title: Why Some People Hear Music That Is Not Playing
summary:
Almost everyone has had a song stuck in their head. But some people hear music that sounds as real as a song on the radio, even when nothing is playing. Scientists call these musical hallucinations.

A hallucination is when the brain senses something that is not really there. Musical hallucinations are sometimes linked to hearing loss. One idea is that when the brain's sound area gets less information from the ears, it pulls music from memory instead.

A new study looked at 80 people who hear music that is not there. Most were older adults, with an average age of 65.

Most of the songs they heard were older songs, not new hits. Religious songs were the most common. Earlier research found many were holiday or children's songs. This suggests the brain reaches back to tunes people learned when they were young.

Only about one in five people could control the music. The researchers hope that explaining the science will help people feel comfortable asking for help.
why_it_matters: Learning how the brain works helps people understand themselves and feel okay asking for help when something feels strange.
